proxy.invalidIpOrHostname: Please enter a valid IP address or hostname
proxy.bindAddressHelp: 0.0.0.0 allows all network access, 127.0.0.1 for local only
proxy.httpsEnabledHelp: Adds a TLS listener for clients that refuse plain HTTP (e.g. Claude Desktop). The HTTP port keeps working.
proxy.httpsPortHelp: Must differ from the HTTP port
proxy.httpsPortConflict: HTTPS port must differ from the HTTP port
proxy.httpsClientUrlHelp: This is the gateway's own https listener (the direct-connection view). The address a client actually uses depends on the access path: store it as the entry's "Client HTTPS URL" in the shell; client switches read that entry value.
proxy.httpsCertNotGenerated: The certificate is generated the first time the proxy starts with HTTPS
proxy.httpsTrustRemoved: Certificate removed from the trust store
proxy.httpsInstallTrustHelp: Writes to the current user's Trusted Root store; the OS shows one confirmation and no administrator rights are needed. Affects only clients that read the system trust store (Claude Desktop, browsers). Restart the client afterwards.
proxy.httpsCertPairRequired: Certificate and private key must be provided together
proxy.httpsCertPathPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the generated certificate
proxy.httpsKeyPathPlaceholder: Provide it together with the certificate
proxy.httpsSanHostsHelp: List the address remote clients actually connect to; localhost / 127.0.0.1 / ::1 are always included. Changing this reissues the certificate, so install the trust once more.
proxy.httpsSanInvalid: Not a valid IP or hostname
proxy.httpsRemoteTrustHint: The certificate has to be trusted on the machine that runs the client. Inside the console that is the block above; on any other computer, fetch the same PEM with GET /v1/management/tls/ca and install it there.
proxy.httpsHandshakeCount: {{total}} since the listener started, {{certificate}} of them certificate rejections ({{codes}})
proxy.httpsNodeClientEnv: For Node-based clients on the gateway machine
proxy.httpsNodeClientHelp: Node clients (Codex CLI, the WorkBuddy/CodeBuddy agent, anything built on node:https or undici) never read the system trust store - they trust their bundled CA set plus NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. Point that variable at this file and restart the client.
proxy.httpsCaCopyFailed: Could not write to the clipboard
proxy.httpsHandshakeGatewayNote: Counted on the gateway machine: a handshake refused by a client never became a request row there.
proxy.httpsMachineTrustPublic: The client https handshake succeeds: the certificate is publicly trusted or already installed - nothing to install.
proxy.httpsMachineNodeEnv: For Node-based clients on this computer
proxy.httpsMachineUnavailable: The console has not read the gateway certificate yet, so this computer has nothing to trust.
proxy.httpsMachineInstallHelp: Writes to the current user's Trusted Root store on this computer only; the gateway machine keeps whatever it already has. Check the fingerprint before installing, and restart the client afterwards.
proxy.httpsMachineManual: This platform has no trust command the console can run: add the certificate above with the system tool, then compare the fingerprint.
proxy.httpsBootstrapHint: If HTTPS itself will not load, the console's connection-failure page offers the same install - an untrusted certificate leaves no page to click a button on.
proxy.fixFormErrors: Please fix the errors in the form
proxy.loadBalanceConfigDesc: Configure account selection strategy and weight distribution
proxy.roundRobinDesc: Use each available account in sequence for even request distribution
proxy.fillFirstDesc: Prioritize current account until limit reached, then switch to next
proxy.failoverDesc: Automatically skip failed accounts. Switch to other accounts after 3 consecutive failures, auto-recover after 1 minute
proxy.smartDesc: Prefer the account whose quota renews soonest, so allowance about to reset gets used instead of wasted
proxy.paceDesc: Prefer the account with the most allowance left per hour until its window resets
proxy.repetitionGuardDesc: Marks a streamed answer whose trailing lines collapsed into duplicates as a degraded success: the scorer stops treating it as a clean win and the conversation is not pinned to that model. The shipped default is calibrated on 99 real reasoning blocks (healthy median 1.000; 0.80 flags 9 of them).
proxy.repetitionGuardMaxRatioHelp: Unique lines / total lines over the trailing window, at or below this counts as degenerate. The client-side guard aborted at 0.35, so the gateway stays deliberately looser and never condemns a stream the client accepted.
proxy.repetitionGuardNonStreamNote: Streaming responses only. A non-streaming response has no per-chunk signal and its body is kept only when body logging is on, so that path is deliberately not judged.
proxy.weightHelp: Higher weight means higher probability of selection. Only effective in round-robin strategy.
proxy.autoRoutingModelScopeHelp: Single: one model per turn; only its accounts fail over, and a different model is reached between turns. Family: same-named models across providers join in. Pool: the old behaviour - a turn may move to another model, which is slower and the next model may read the tool protocol differently
proxy.autoRoutingMaxAttemptsHelp: How many candidates one request may try before it gives up on account-level failures (5xx, network). Recoverable rejections - queueing, quota, a model this channel no longer serves - keep switching until the wall-clock budget instead (40s single-model, 90s whole pool), and are not capped at this number
proxy.autoRoutingStickyHelp: Reuse the model that last succeeded for the same conversation within this window; set to 0 to disable
proxy.autoRoutingStickyHardPin: Hard-pin the sticky model (route it first regardless of score)
proxy.autoRoutingStickyHardPinHelp: On: the model this conversation last succeeded on is moved to the front of the candidate list, so an agent session does not change model mid-task. Off: stickiness is only a score bonus (+0.12, or +0.06 for another account of the same model), and a clearly better candidate wins it.
proxy.autoRoutingStickyHardPinIdle: Stickiness is already off (the window above is 0), so this setting does nothing right now.
proxy.autoRoutingFairnessHelp: How far a model may run ahead of the least-dispatched model in this route's pool before it moves behind every model that has served less. 0 rotates strictly; 2 (the default) lets one model serve three dispatches in a row; 20 is effectively score-only. Conversation stickiness still keeps one session on one model. Every candidate in the pool is now ranked - nothing is capped to one model per provider - so this is what decides whether the tail of the pool ever gets a turn.
proxy.autoRoutingPreferHelp: Balanced picks a tier from the request complexity, Fast prefers quick models, Strong prefers capable ones, Cheap prefers free or low-multiplier models. The X-Auto-Prefer header overrides it per request
proxy.addAndActivateAccount: Please add and activate accounts first
proxy.timeoutHelp: Maximum wait time for a single request (1-300 seconds)
proxy.retryCountMustBeNumber: Retry count must be a number
proxy.retryCountHelp: Automatic retry count after request failure (0-10 times)
proxy.outputCapFallbackHelp: The Anthropic protocol requires max_tokens: when the client sends neither spelling and no per-model parameter is set, this value is used. Leave empty for the built-in default of 4096.
proxy.outputCapMustBeInteger: Output cap must be an integer
proxy.outputCapRangeError: Output cap must be between 1 and 1000000
proxy.restartRequiredDesc: Port or bind address has changed. The proxy service needs to restart for the changes to take effect. Restart now?
proxy.proxyRestarted: Proxy service has been restarted with new configuration
proxy.autoRoutingPoolStrategyHelp: Check strategies to keep only models that satisfy them. Strategies target models, not accounts, so all accounts of one model are filtered together. No selection means no filtering.
proxy.autoRoutingPoolStrategy_multimodal_desc: Accepts image input (currently approximated by vision)
proxy.autoRoutingPoolStrategy_reasoning_desc: Strong tier and name contains reason/thinking
proxy.autoRoutingPoolStrategy_annotated-only_d: At least one capability is explicitly annotated
proxy.autoRoutingPoolStrategy_cost-known_desc: Cost bucket is neither unknown nor missing
proxy.autoRoutingPoolOperatorHelp: Operators apply left to right: And intersects, Or unions. The first strategy operator is ignored.
proxy.modelRoutesDesc: A route is a named request-time pool decision: send its name as the model and candidates are filtered and ranked with this scoring strategy, preference, attempt cap and pool filters. The pool is recomputed from the models served right now on every request, so adding or removing a model needs no route edit.
proxy.modelRoutesEmptyHelp: Create one and use its name as the model in requests; the route named auto came from the legacy automatic routing config.
proxy.routesUnavailable: The routes API is unavailable; restart the app and try again
proxy.routesLoadFailed: Failed to load the route list
proxy.routeNameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, underscore and hyphen, at most 64 characters; it must not clash with an existing route, model name or user alias.
proxy.routeStrategyHelp: Sets only how this route ranks its candidates; the account pick inside a provider still follows the server-wide strategy above.
proxy.routeRenameHelp: Type a new name to rename it: requests have to use the new name from then on and the old one stops resolving at once.
proxy.routeDeleteWarning_auto: After deleting it, /v1/models stops advertising auto and model="auto" resolves as a plain model name again (no longer a route); if no model carries that name, clients get an unknown-model error.
proxy.routeDeleteWarning_other: After deleting it, /v1/models stops advertising "{{name}}" and requests naming it resolve as a plain model name again (no longer a route); if no model carries that name, clients get an unknown-model error.
proxy.routeUpdatedToast: Route state updated and effective immediately
proxy.routeImmediateHelp: Creating, editing, renaming, toggling and deleting a route persists at once and takes effect on the next request - no proxy restart needed.
proxy.routeAttemptsSummary: Up to {{attempts}} failovers on account-level failures
proxy.routePoolSize: {{count}} model(s) currently in this route's pool
proxy.routePoolSizeEmpty: This route's pool is empty: it is still advertised on /v1/models, but every request to it fails with 503. Loosen its pool strategies, or start more models on the Models page.
proxy.routePoolSizeUnknown: Pool size unavailable (could not read the current catalogue)
proxy.routePoolHelp: The preview runs the same collection/strategy/manual pipeline as a real request and shows where each model ends up. Models wrongly dropped by a strategy can be added back by hand; models you never want picked can be removed. Manual overrides never bypass request hard filters (image → vision, context) or contract filters.
proxy.routePinSummary: Pinned pool: this route can only serve these {{total}} model name(s).
proxy.routeMinTier: Capability floor (serve this tier and above)
proxy.routeMinTierHelp: Models below this tier are dropped for the whole route, and the floor runs before pool strategies and manual includes - neither can bring one back. Use it when the pool is all free/small models and you want at least a mid tier. The tier comes from capability marks; an unmarked model falls back to a name heuristic, never to unknown.
proxy.routeBasedOnHelp: Pick an existing route and this route takes its candidate pool, strategies, name pin and manual include/exclude verbatim from it. References are one hop only, so 'A borrows B which borrows C' cannot happen. This is how you give one pool a second client-facing name (an Anthropic tier, say) without copying a config that would then drift apart.
proxy.routeBasedOnNotice: Everything about how this route selects comes from '{{route}}'; the strategies and manual include/exclude below do not run. Clear the reference to edit those.
proxy.routeBasedOnSummary: Pool comes from {{route}} (the strategies above are not executed by this route)
proxy.routePoolSummary: Candidates {{candidates}} · after strategies {{afterStrategies}} · after manual fixes {{afterManual}} · unavailable {{unavailable}}
proxy.routePoolConflict: "{{strategy}}" joined with "or" re-admits {{count}} candidates that fail the strategies before it ({{broken}}): those no longer constrain this pool.
proxy.routePoolEmpty: No routable model under the current configuration ({{reasons}})
proxy.routePoolMissing_min_tier: the capability floor emptied the pool
proxy.routePoolUnresolved: {{count}} manually added model(s) are no longer candidates (stopped or deleted); remove them individually
proxy.routePoolMarkHelp: Manual marks win over everything and survive model syncs. "Inherit" keeps the automatic result (provider record / aggregate official / static table / third-party / name heuristic).
proxy.routePoolMarkContextTooLarge: Context window must not exceed {{max}} tokens.
proxy.routePoolMarkMaxOutputHelp: Unit: tokens. Leave blank to leave it unmarked (never stored as 0); positive whole numbers only, up to {{max}}.
proxy.routePoolMarkMaxOutputInvalid: Enter a positive whole number of tokens (digits only, not 0 or a decimal).
proxy.routePoolMarkMaxOutputTooLarge: Max output must not exceed {{max}} tokens.
proxy.routePoolMarkModalitiesHelp: Leave all unchecked to inherit; once checked, this set is authoritative.
proxy.routePoolMarkWeightHelp: Leave blank to inherit the automatic source (scored as unknown, never treated as free). 0 means free. Non-negative decimals accepted, up to {{max}}.
proxy.routePoolMarkWeightInvalid: Enter a non-negative number (e.g. 0.5 or 2); negatives and non-numbers are rejected.
proxy.routePoolMarkFreeHelp: Marking the model free scores it in the free bucket, ahead of the multiplier. “Inherit” keeps using the automatic sources.

gatewayUpdate.title: Docker gateway online update
gatewayUpdate.desc: Downloads the official release image, verifies SHA-256, then a one-shot helper container performs stop-old → start-new → probe → rollback-on-failure. Requires docker.sock mounted at deploy time.

compression.title: Context compression
compression.loading: Reading the current settings… (no switch until the stored value arrives, so a default can never be saved as if it were the user's choice)
compression.enableHint: Compresses only the newest turn (tool output and user input) and leaves all history bytes untouched, so the upstream prompt cache is preserved. With it off, requests are byte-for-byte unchanged.
compression.aggressivenessHint: Stronger settings keep fewer rows. Error rows, statistical outliers and numeric anomalies are never dropped at any strength.
compression.cacheFirst: Cache first (skip compression for cache-friendly providers)
compression.cacheFirstHint: A compressed block is discarded by the next turn's original bytes, so on providers whose cached input is much cheaper than fresh input (DeepSeek, Anthropic) compression usually costs more than it saves. This policy skips it unless a per-provider override says otherwise.
compression.outputContractHint: Nothing is injected by default. On "Concise" or "Minimal", a fixed system block is placed before requests that carry tools, asking for fewer words. It turns itself off for a target that has produced degraded turns (looping, empty turn, announcing work it never does) — at that point the evidence is that this model does not follow the instruction.
compression.foldDuplicates: Fold repeated history (replace a duplicate message with a retrievable pointer)
compression.foldDuplicatesHint: When a whole message matches an earlier one line for line, the later copy becomes a pointer and the original stays retrievable locally. Rewriting history costs one prompt-cache miss, so it only runs when the measurement gate passes: at least 20% duplication, a conclusive log window, and at least 2 more turns expected in the conversation.

promptCaching.title: Prompt cache
promptCaching.enableHint: Adds cache_control markers to Anthropic-format requests (tool list, system prompt, previous turn). Metadata only — no text is changed. Implicit-cache providers such as DeepSeek need no marker and are unaffected.
promptCaching.ttlHint: 5 minutes is the default tier. 1 hour costs more to write but survives longer gaps; it is only sent to endpoints that support explicit breakpoints.
promptCaching.note: Anthropic-format endpoints only. DeepSeek and other implicit-prefix providers cache automatically; their hit rate is governed by prefix stability and account/model affinity, not this switch.
promptCaching.configSaveFailed: Failed to save prompt cache settings

anthropicInbound.title: Anthropic clients (Claude Desktop / Claude Code)
anthropicInbound.documentPassThroughHint: Anthropic `document` blocks become OpenAI-compatible `file` parts and really reach the upstream. On (the default) means a model that cannot read files fails loudly instead of answering as though nothing was attached - and because an attachment counts as a vision need, such a request only routes to candidates marked vision-capable. Off drops the block but records it in X-ModelPort-Anthropic-Dropped plus a warning log. The switch is read by proxy/routes/messages.ts.
anthropicInbound.defaultModelHint: Where a request lands when the model name the client sent cannot be resolved in the gateway. Leave it empty to use the gateway default: the `auto` route, or the first enabled route when there is no `auto`.
anthropicInbound.mappingsHint: Name sent by the client (exact name or prefix) → gateway model. Exact keys take precedence over prefixes.
anthropicInbound.noMappings: No mapping yet: a name the gateway does not recognize falls through to the fallback model above.
anthropicInbound.discoveryHint: Claude Desktop and Claude Code keep only model IDs starting with claude or anthropic when they read /v1/models, so a real Claude model advertised as <entry>/<model> disappears from the client. /v1/models advertises routes only, so this creates one route per such model, named by the Anthropic ID already in the gateway's data, with its candidate pool pinned to the entries that actually serve it — never an invented name, never a route free to answer with any model. This section only serves installs whose catalogue really contains a Claude-shaped model; when none exists the section is not rendered at all, and the tier list above is the way in.
anthropicInbound.discoverySkipped: {{total}} name(s) skipped, each with its reason:
anthropicInbound.discoveryFailed: {{total}} route(s) could not be created; the ones already created stay in place:
anthropicInbound.discoveryNothingNew: Nothing to create: every discoverable name already has a route.

discoveryReason.no-active-account: that provider has no active account, so the name would be dead on arrival
discoveryReason.already-visible: a model with that name already exists
discoveryReason.mapping-exists: an alias owns that name, and a route may not collide with one
discoveryReason.route-name-taken: a route with that name already exists
discoveryReason.name-not-routable: the Anthropic ID contains a dot or a slash, which route names cannot carry (the name goes into the X-ModelPort-Route-Name header) - use Model Mapping to point it at a route

anthropicInbound.duplicateNames: Repeated client name: {{names}} — only the last row takes effect.
anthropicInbound.discoveryNote: A row whose left-hand name is a complete model name is also advertised on /v1/models, so the client can pick it from its own list. A prefix-only key (for example `claude-`) is used for matching but can never appear in that list, because the client filters every row against Anthropic's own model-name table.
anthropicInbound.tierTitle: Advertise routes by Anthropic family tier
anthropicInbound.tierHint: Claude Desktop keeps a row when its id is a model name it knows, or when the row carries a legal family tier. So tagging an existing route with a tier advertises it without inventing Anthropic names; the client sends that route name back and the request lands in that route's own pool. That covers discovery only: its model picker re-filters by name and a tier does not count there, so the rows it cannot select are listed below.
anthropicInbound.tierNoRoutes: No enabled routes: enable one on the Routes page first.
anthropicInbound.routeColumn: Route name (this is what the client filters on)
anthropicInbound.surfaceLead: Two tables, two jobs: "client name -> gateway route" decides which names appear in Claude and which route each one runs; "advertise routes by Anthropic family tier" decides which family a route stands in for, and its last column states the outcome. The client only trusts names - a route whose name is not Anthropic-shaped is discoverable but not selectable.
anthropicInbound.outcomeNeedsName: Discovered but not selectable today - saving renames it to {{name}}
anthropicInbound.outcomeNotAdvertised: Never listed: no tier, and {{name}} is not an Anthropic-shaped name
anthropicInbound.pickerGapAuto: Saving appends these to the mapping table above: {{pairs}} (names are claude-<tier> with no version number, so nothing pretends to be a specific Anthropic release; edit or delete them there)
anthropicInbound.pickerGapBlocked: No free name could be generated for: {{names}} — rename those routes yourself
anthropicInbound.pickerGapFix: To choose different names, rename the routes instead (for example claude-daily) - each row restates its outcome afterwards.
